quarterly_data.signal: DEFERRED REVENUE CONVERSION IS GATED BY DATA CENTER READINESS: CFO Chantelle Breithaupt said product deferred revenue is already shipped, invoiced and usually cash-collected, and converts only on customer acceptance - which can take 18 to 24 months because of power, cooling, facilities and cabling readiness. She gave a live example of a large customer whose data center construction stopped for a three to four-week delay after an employee injury. Deferred revenue today is the new use cases: scale-out, scale-across, eventually scale-up, 800G and 1.6T.
quarterly_data.figure: 18 to 24 months; three to four-week delay

quarterly_data.signal: PRICE INCREASE MECHANICS AND A TARIFF TAILWIND INSIDE THE MARGIN GUIDE: Breithaupt said the single FY2026 price increase was curated, not blanket - applied only to future POs of customers whose bill of material carried a significant component, where 'the largest component is the memory' - and was sized to hold, not accrete, gross margin. It was applied 'only to POs in the future', so the increases land only as backlog works through into new purchase orders. Inside the 62-64 gross margin guide, roughly 30 basis points on the year is a one-time tariff refund flowing back into the P&L. She would not commit to whether a second price increase is needed in 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: 30 basis points; 62-64 guide; the largest component is the memory

quarterly_data.signal: NEOCLOUD CREDIT DISCIPLINE (NOT DISCUSSED ON THE CALL): Breithaupt described NeoClouds as 'almost like a high-risk, high-reward segment', said the segment is not always proven out from a financial backing perspective, and that Arista therefore either walks away from the deal or uses prepayment scenarios - being explicit about where the invoice gets paid, because many NeoClouds start and not all make it. Duda added NeoClouds are an ideal Arista customer because their mandate is lowest token cost, which pushes them to best-of-breed rather than single-vendor lock-in.
